root_cause.text: The use of radix_tree for qrtr_tx_flow in the QRTR network subsystem creates a memory leak because __radix_tree_create() can leave orphaned internal nodes in the tree if a later allocation fails, and the cleanup code using radix_tree_for_each_slot() only frees leaf entries, not internal nodes.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message states: "__radix_tree_create() allocates and links intermediate nodes into the tree one by one. If a subsequent allocation fails, the already-linked nodes remain in the tree with no corresponding leaf entry. These orphaned internal nodes are never reclaimed because radix_tree_for_each_slot() only visits slots containing leaf values." The patch migrates to xarray, where xa_destroy() properly frees all internal nodes.

vuln_statements.explanation: radix_tree_insert can allocate internal nodes via __radix_tree_create; if the insertion fails after partial allocation, those internal nodes become orphaned because the subsequent kfree only frees the leaf flow entry.

This kfree is executed when radix_tree_insert fails; it only frees the leaf flow structure and does not clean up any internal nodes that may have been allocated during the insertion attempt, leading to a memory leak.

This deletion call removes only the leaf entry from the tree; it does not free internal nodes that may have been orphaned, contributing to the memory leak.
